clue.text: Treatment of an entire individual measure of alcohol is medicinal

indicators.note: a measure is a portion, so a portion of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits taken as a remedy for what ails you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure of alcohol' reads as a dram, but 'measure of' signals a portion of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The holistic approach in medicine treats the whole person, mind and body, rather than single symptoms.

clue.text: Top removed from hut made an observation tool

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a hut is taken off

parts.note: a shack is a rough hut
saw means observed, made an observation

explanation.surface: Someone takes the roof off a shed to build a lookout instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observation tool' wants to be a telescope; only 'tool' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting metal, a workshop implement.

clue.text: Tempted to have iodine for energy — sensational!

indicators.note: the word is made to take on a new letter in place of another
for marks the swap: one letter put in place of the other

parts.note: lured means tempted
E is the physics symbol for energy
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Someone lured into something racy finds it thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes something shocking and sensational, like a tabloid headline.

clue.text: Put off by The Simpsons and the like, which is not much of an existence

parts.note: to suspend something is to put it off, postpone it
The Simpsons is a cartoon series, an example of animated film

explanation.surface: Watching cartoons all day is a barely living, dormant sort of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off by' reads as disliking the show; 'Put off' is a synonym for postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the state of a living thing with its vital functions halted, alive yet barely living.

clue.text: Mobile medical spout

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters of the next word are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A mobile medical unit, or a burst of speech from a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to hold forth pompously, which is what one does when one orates loudly.

clue.text: Tearing hip

definitions.meaning: tearing here means rushing about at speed
hip means stylish and fashionable, as is a dapper figure

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rushing along fast and attractively stylish.

clue.text: In France, Le Blanc is a tabloid target

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A French person called Le Blanc is being pursued by the gutter press.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous personality is just what the tabloid press chases for stories.

clue.text: See 3
He scored Harlem Winds

indicators.note: winds read as a verb, twists and turns, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A jazz musician wrote music for the wind section of a Harlem band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like the woodwind section; it is a verb, twists.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was an Austrian composer, a man who wrote orchestral scores.

clue.text: Sounding most upper-class and Victoria-like?

definitions.meaning: a posh, rich voice is described with this word
the Victoria is a common British variety of plum, so plum-like

explanation.definitionFit: A voice with this quality sounds posh; the word also means full of or like plums, such as the Victoria variety.

clue.text: Rocky lays into Patten, flier of the future?

indicators.note: into says one set of letters goes inside the other

parts.note: Chris Patten, the British politician and last governor of Hong Kong

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of the next word are shaken up

explanation.surface: A boxer called Rocky floors a politician called Patten.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa encased before becoming a butterfly or moth is a future winged insect.

clue.text: Secure backing to break left hand somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: a word that breaks another splits it open by sitting inside it
backing means going backwards, so the word for secure is read from the end

parts.note: to tie is to secure

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fasten a splint to break an injured left hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure' reads as an adjective; it is the verb, and 'backing' turns it round before it goes between the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith is the port district of Edinburgh, a real place in Scotland.

clue.text: Grass spades advantage

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: A gardener's spades give an advantage on the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant of marshy ground.

clue.text: See 27
Week remains Doris's cleaning time?

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
Doris Day, the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A week in which a woman named Doris stays put, looked at as a time for chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry day, traditionally Monday, is the day set aside for doing the household washing.

clue.text: Reduction of hard bowls area set in green

indicators.note: set in says the next letters are placed inside the colour word

parts.note: sage is a greyish-green colour
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
a rink is a strip of a bowling green used for one game of bowls

explanation.surface: A tough bowling rink is laid out within the green.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowls is a British lawn game; 'green' looks like the bowling green but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is the amount by which something has got smaller, a decrease.

clue.text: Game sacrifice of good compass

parts.note: compass in the sense of range or scope is ambit

explanation.surface: Giving up a piece in a game, as one gives up a good compass.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess an opening where a pawn is given up for an advantage has this name.

clue.text: Upturned stone with top marking young man's pile of money?

indicators.note: in a down light, upturned means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
A is the highest grade a piece of work can be marked
a buck is a dashing young man; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: A rich young man's fortune topped with a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a very large sum, a fortune in cash.

clue.text: A sum for recording Believe?

definitions.meaning: an entry in the plus column of accounts records a sum received
to believe someone is to give them credence

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a payment entry in a ledger and a verb meaning to accept as true.

clue.text: Run against the blue opponent of Stalinism

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace
the blue is a poetic term for the sky

explanation.surface: A runner set against a blue political opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the blue' looks like a Tory (blue in UK politics), but it is the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was Stalin's great rival in the Soviet leadership, later exiled and murdered.

clue.text: Cry off limiting gene modification in a certain style

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, holding the other letters within bounds
off means awry, so the letters of the word are rearranged
a modification is a change, so the letters of the word are altered in order

explanation.surface: Calling off genetic tinkering in a particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cry off' looks like the phrase meaning withdraw, but 'off' just scrambles the first word, and 'modification' scrambles the second, which sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Regency is a British decorative and architectural style of the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: Regulation about Spanish article for space between bed and wall

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a rule is a regulation
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A rule about the Spanish word for the, oddly tied to bedroom space.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruelle is the narrow gap between a bed and the wall, once a French salon setting.

clue.text: A team, or those who have been pulled out?

definitions.meaning: the New York baseball club is a famous American sports team

definitions.text: those who have been pulled out?
definitions.meaning: to yank is to pull sharply, so people yanked out would be ..., in a whimsical sense

explanation.definitionFit: The New York baseball side bears this name; read whimsically it means people who have been yanked.

clue.text: Outlandish, ultimately futile kiss on the ear

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A pointless peck on someone's ear seems bizarre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreign and strange, out of the ordinary, is described with this word.

clue.text: Who dislikes foreign types of plastic phone boxes no end

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters are remoulded into a new order
no end says the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes plastic phone boxes of foreign kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts BOXES to BOXE; with PHONE, 'plastic' rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with an irrational fear or hatred of foreigners.

clue.text: See 24
Brunette, possibly with daily application for Jack's sore top?

parts.note: a brunette has hair of a dark colour such as brown
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: A brunette reading the daily press, or a nursery remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'Jack and Jill', Jack broke his crown and bound his head with vinegar and brown paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme has Jack treat his injured head with vinegar and this wrapping material, a folk remedy.

clue.text: American western type of hat bishop discarded

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop throws away his straw hat in the Wild West.
explanation.definitionFit: Oater is US slang for a cowboy film, after the oats fed to horses.

clue.text: Crossword setter's craft

definitions.meaning: The pseudonym of a Guardian crossword compiler
a ... steamer is a cargo ship, a seagoing craft

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fellow Guardian setter and a cargo ship without fixed route.

clue.text: Unite ocean couple and have a drink

parts.note: to splice ropes is to unite them by interweaving
the main is a poetic term for the open ocean
a brace is a pair, a couple

explanation.surface: Join the sea and a pair, then take a tot.
explanation.definitionFit: This naval phrase originally meant an extra rum ration and now means to have a celebratory drink.

clue.text: As is evident, its heart is quite a different organ

parts.words: its heart is quite a different organ
parts.note: the middle three letters of the word form a hearing organ, not a heart at all

explanation.surface: Plainly, this thing's heart is not a heart at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the answer word, its central letters, spells an organ of hearing: quite different from a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plain to see, so it is so obviously, without doubt.

clue.text: Very backward name of female god

indicators.note: backward means read from the end, so the word is turned round

parts.note: so means very
Iris is a woman's given name

explanation.surface: A goddess's name written very backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female god' wants to be the definition, but Osiris is male; 'female' goes with 'name of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian deity of the afterlife and the dead.
